bindings.label: Patient presented with stridor, increased work of breathing, and supplemental oxygen requirement.

A man presented to the emergency department on transfer from an outside hospital after falling with an e-cigarette in his mouth several hours earlier; he did not remember the exact cause of the fall but believed he may have lost consciousness.
Physical examination in the ED showed diffuse supraglottic edema most severe in the epiglottis, arytenoids, and aryepiglottic folds, obstructing a view of the true vocal cords.
CT shows glottic and supraglottic swelling without fracture
Direct laryngoscopy shows diffuse edema and sloughing of pharyngeal and supraglottic mucosa, most severe in epiglottis
Acute supraglottic edema due to e-cigarette airway injury
Bronchoscopy and inflammatory markers remain unavailable
CT and direct laryngoscopy show no fracture and no infectious features
